title: Q1. Connections Between Locations
question: Which city-level locations connect to the ISP? Explain whether these locations necessarily belong to the same LAN.
steps: Return to the city-level Logical workspace.
Trace the links attached to ISP.
Identify Office, Library, Home and any completed Second Home connection.
prompt: List the connected locations and explain LAN versus WAN.

title: Q2. Second Home WAN Interface
question: Investigate which ISP device, port and cable connect to Second Home.
steps: At city level, inspect the Second Home–ISP link.
Enter ISP if needed to inspect Cloud0.
Record the exact interface and media type.
prompt: Record Cloud0 interface, connected modem port and cable type.

title: Q3. Office Router Addressing
question: Inspect Office-RT. Record three configured router interfaces/subinterfaces and their IPv4 addresses and masks. Why does the router need multiple interfaces?
steps: Enter Office in Logical view.
Click Office-RT → Config or CLI.
Inspect G0/0/0.2, G0/0/0.20 and G0/0/1; compare with the topology notes.
prompt: Record the three interfaces and explain their routing role.

title: Q4. LAN Expansion Using Switches
question: Identify the central Office switch and additional switches. Explain how the added switch extends the LAN.
steps: In Office, locate Office-SW1, Office-SW2 and Office-SW3.
Click switches or inspect their port connections.
Identify the uplink path and its significance.
prompt: Name the switches, identify the main switch and explain LAN expansion.

title: Q5. Office-User IP Configuration
question: Determine the Office-User IP address, subnet mask, gateway and DHCP/static mode. Compare with Office-Admin.
steps: Click Office-User → Desktop → IP Configuration.
Record IP, subnet mask, default gateway and DHCP/Static selection.
Repeat on Office-Admin and compare.
prompt: Record actual settings from both PCs and one comparison.

title: Q6. Office-to-Office Ping
question: Test whether Office-User can reach Office-Admin. Record the actual destination IP and the ping outcome.
steps: Check Office-Admin → Desktop → IP Configuration to confirm its current IP.
Office-User → Desktop → Command Prompt.
Run ping to the confirmed Office-Admin IP (the activity instructions suggest ping 192.168.20.5).
Record success/failure and explain ICMP.
prompt: Give command, IP verification, observed result and explanation.

title: Q7. Office Web Service
question: From Office-User, access office.srv. If it works, what else has been verified besides ping?
steps: Office-User → Desktop → Web Browser.
Enter http://office.srv or office.srv.
Record what happens; if unsuccessful, check addressing, DNS and server services.
prompt: Describe the observed result and DNS/HTTP significance.

title: Q8. Library Device Inventory
question: Inventory the Library cluster. Classify devices as end devices, intermediary devices or servers.
steps: Back Level → City → Library.
Count visible devices and record their names.
Classify each device type from its actual role.
prompt: Report device inventory and classifications from Packet Tracer.

title: Q9. Library Addressing
question: Inspect a Library end device's IP, mask, gateway and configuration mode. Compare its subnet with the Office network.
steps: Select a Library PC (or equivalent end device).
For PC: Desktop → IP Configuration.
Compare observed address/mask with Office-User.
prompt: Record actual values and reason whether the subnet is the same.

title: Q10. Cluster and Uncluster
question: What changes, and what remains unchanged, when Library devices are unclustered and re-clustered?
steps: Save a working copy of the .pka activity.
At City level, select Library → Delete → Uncluster (NOT Delete).
Select the expanded devices → Create New Cluster (Shift+U) → rename Library.
prompt: Describe visual changes and explain whether IP addressing or forwarding changes.

title: Q11. Home Device and ISP Path
question: Identify the devices inside the existing Home cluster and trace their connection toward the ISP.
steps: Back Level → City → Home.
Record all observed network devices and end devices.
Trace an end-device path to the ISP.
prompt: Write the device names and connection path you actually observed.

title: Q12. Home IP Allocation
question: Determine whether a selected Home PC/laptop gets network settings using DHCP or Static configuration.
steps: Home → choose a PC or laptop.
Desktop → IP Configuration.
Record IP address, subnet mask, gateway and configuration mode.
prompt: Give observed configuration values and one advantage of DHCP.

title: Q13. Compare Home and Office
question: Give two evidence-based differences between the existing Home cluster and Office cluster.
steps: Inspect the existing Home topology.
Back Level → Office and inspect network devices.
Compare device types, topology structure, wireless systems or address ranges.
prompt: Describe two observed differences, citing the device evidence.

title: Q14. Three Core Home Devices
question: Identify the three required devices in Second Home and explain their distinct roles.
steps: At city level enter Second Home (create it first if needed).
Locate PC0, Home Gateway1 and Cable Modem0.
Inspect the device names and interfaces.
prompt: Explain the purpose of PC, Home Gateway and Cable Modem.

title: Q15. Verify LAN Cabling
question: Record exact ports and cable types for PC0 → Home Gateway1 → Cable Modem0.
steps: Inspect the PC0 to Home Gateway1 cable.
Inspect the Home Gateway1 to Cable Modem0 cable.
Record both interface pairs and cable media.
prompt: State each source port, destination port and cable type.

title: Q16. Explore Home Gateway Interfaces
question: What is the difference between Home Gateway1's Ethernet (LAN) and Internet (WAN) interfaces?
steps: Second Home → Home Gateway1.
Inspect Config or GUI → LAN/Ethernet and Internet settings.
Identify the interface facing PC0 and the interface facing Cable Modem0.
prompt: Describe LAN/WAN sides and your observed settings.

title: Q17. Connect Second Home to ISP
question: Verify how the Cable Modem connects to the ISP. Does a connected cable alone prove Internet reachability?
steps: Return to City and inspect the Second Home–ISP connection.
Check Cable Modem0 Port 0 → Cloud0 Coaxial9.
Distinguish physical connectivity from IP/application connectivity.
prompt: Record connection details and explain why cabling alone is insufficient.

title: Q18. Compare All Five Clusters
question: Compare ISP, Office, Library, Home and Second Home by device type, function and ISP connection.
steps: Return to City → visit each of the five clusters.
Inspect at least one key networking device per cluster.
Summarize the five locations with actual evidence.
prompt: Write five brief cluster summaries and one major difference.

title: Q19. Simulation Mode
question: Use Simulation Mode to observe a PDU between Office-User and Office-Admin. Which protocols/events appear?
steps: Office → switch Realtime to Simulation.
Choose Add Simple PDU (envelope), source Office-User, destination Office-Admin.
Press Capture/Forward and examine Event List and PDU Details.
prompt: Record at least two observed packet events and explain the result.

title: Q20. Troubleshooting Strategy
question: Suppose Office-User cannot reach Office-Admin. Describe and demonstrate a systematic troubleshooting sequence.
steps: Check links and interface status.
Verify Office-User and Office-Admin IP/mask/gateway settings.
Ping the correct destination; use Simulation Mode for deeper inspection.
prompt: Write a diagnostic sequence with evidence and likely causes.
